answer: To resist sybils, each agent locks a bond that is slashed whenever two identities share a funding source or vote in lockstep. Running a thousand fakes forces an attacker to bridge a thousand separate deposits and pay that stake repeatedly, so mass duplication becomes unprofitable. Trust accrues at the slow pace of a glacier, meaning fresh accounts cannot instantly impersonate long-lived peers. A transient zephyr of throwaway identities therefore earns no voting weight and is discarded at settlement.
